Legal Standards.name: Bay-Delta water quality objectives implemented through water rights (SWRCB)
Legal Standards.note: When storage is low, operators often cannot meet flow/salinity/outflow/export constraint requirements without jeopardizing later health & safety supplies; managed through SWRCB permit/license conditions and Temporary Urgency Change orders.

Legal Standards.name: Temporary Urgency Change authority (SWRCB)
Legal Standards.note: Used when storage is too low to meet permit conditions; allows temporary changes to D-1641-related permit terms to reduce immediate releases and preserve future supplies.

Legal Standards.name: Drought emergency curtailment regulations (SWRCB)
Legal Standards.note: Low storage coincides with hydrologic conditions where SWRCB determines water is not available under priority of right and adopts emergency regulations requiring curtailment/reporting.

Legal Standards.name: Reasonable use / beneficial use limitation (California Constitution)
Legal Standards.note: As storage drops, agencies justify restrictions, conservation mandates, and curtailments under the constitutional requirement to prevent unreasonable use.

Legal Standards.name: Federal environmental allocation/operational requirements (CVP)
Legal Standards.note: CVP operations must reserve/manage water for fish and habitat objectives even in dry years, which becomes harder at low storage.

Legal Standards.name: ESA Section 7 'no jeopardy' constraints on operations
Legal Standards.note: Storage affects ability to meet flow/temperature/export constraints that are part of ESA Reasonable and Prudent Alternatives/Measures for listed species in CVP/SWP operations.

Legal Standards.name: Flood control operating rules/manuals (USACE + dam owners/operators)
Legal Standards.note: Even if water supply storage is good, reservoirs can be legally/operationally constrained by required flood space and water control manuals.

Legal Standards.name: Dam safety reservoir restrictions (DWR Division of Safety of Dams)
Legal Standards.note: Storage may be capped downward by dam safety directives, limiting max reservoir elevation/contents, which directly changes how often it fills.

Tier 1.threshold: Storage >= top threshold in >=90% of years (April values). As of July 2025, top threshold = 50th percentile of recent historical CDEC data.

policies.note: Meeting D-1641 / Bay-Delta Plan flow & operational objectives is generally easier because stored water is available to shape releases and Delta conditions. (D-1641 is the binding standard for SWP/CVP permits.)
ESA/CVPIA operational constraints are generally easier to satisfy (more cold-water pool / release flexibility), lowering the need for emergency deviations.

Flood control operating constraints may still be implicated if April storage is high and late storms occur; USACE/DWR flood manuals can require releases to maintain flood space (not a 'violation,' but a controlling legal/operational regime).

Tier 2.threshold: Storage >= middle threshold in >=67% of years (April values). As of July 2025, middle threshold = 33rd percentile of recent historical CDEC data.

policies.note: D-1641 objectives and ESA/CVPIA requirements are often still achievable, but with tradeoffs (e.g., protecting cold-water pool vs. meeting Delta objectives). D-1641 assigns responsibility to DWR/USBR to meet 'flow-dependent numeric objectives.'

Project allocation and shortage policies become more prominent planning tools. CVP allocations are based on 'amounts of storage in CVP reservoirs, regulatory requirements …' SWP allocation updates (monthly adjustments) are often sensitive to existing storage entering spring/summer.
Tier 2 can be where local/seasonal water quality or temperature limits become tight late summer, depending on inflow and demand (implicating ESA/D-1641 compliance risk).

Tier 3.threshold: Storage >= middle threshold in >=30% of years (April values). As of July 2025, middle threshold = 33rd percentile of recent historical CDEC data.

policies.note: TUCP requests and approvals become more likely when storage/inflow are insufficient to comply with D-1641 while preserving later health & safety supplies. SWRCB's TUCP authority allows petitions for 'a conditional, temporary change order' when 'Projects storage and inflow may not be enough to meet D-1641 requirements.'
Stronger use of shortage allocation policies (CVP) because allocations are explicitly based on forecasted inflows, storage, and regulatory requirements.
Operators may either (a) release more and harm summer storage or (b) seek temporary relaxation via TUCP—meaning D-1641 is directly implicated.
Lower storage reduces flexibility to meet fish flow/temperature measures while also meeting water quality standards.

Tier 4.threshold: Does not meet Tiers 1-3; storage below middle threshold (at or below lower threshold) in >70% of years (April values). As of July 2025, lower threshold = 20th percentile of recent historical values.

policies.note: SWRCB can find water is unavailable under priority and/or unreasonable use must be prevented. Emergency regulation can 'require curtailment of diversions when water is not available under the diverter's priority of right.'

TUCP filings/approvals to temporarily change SWP/CVP permit conditions (often explicitly to deviate from D-1641 objectives to preserve minimum supplies), because storage shortfalls are a standard justification.

policies.policy_name: Severe project delivery reductions / shortage allocations
policies.note: Severe project delivery reductions / shortage allocations (CVP and often SWP), because storage is a stated input to allocation decisions.

policies.relationship: Most likely violated / unable to meet without relief
policies.note: Tier 4 conditions often make it infeasible to meet all flow-dependent objectives and preserve later supplies, which is exactly why TUCPs seek temporary changes to 'conditions imposed pursuant to… D-1641.'

policies.relationship: Most likely violated / unable to meet without relief
policies.note: ESA/CVPIA operational measures become harder to implement (e.g., cold-water pool protection vs. required releases). CVPIA (b)(2) dedicates project yield for environmental purposes, which competes with deliveries in dry storage years.

policies.policy_name: Constitutional reasonable use / Dam safety restrictions
policies.note: Constitutional 'reasonable use' justification for strict conservation and limits in severe scarcity. If 'low storage' is due to dam safety restrictions (i.e., storage is capped), DSOD reservoir restriction authorities can be the direct cause of Tier 4 outcomes for that reservoir.

Governing Agencies.name: SWRCB (State Water Board)
Governing Agencies.note: Water rights permits/licenses; D-1641 implementation; TUCP orders; drought emergency regulations/curtailments.

Governing Agencies.name: DWR
Governing Agencies.note: SWP operations and allocations; reservoir/flood operations for state facilities; DSOD dam safety oversight.

Governing Agencies.name: USBR (Reclamation)
Governing Agencies.note: CVP operations and allocations; CVPIA implementation.

Governing Agencies.name: USACE
Governing Agencies.note: Flood control rules/water control manuals and water control management framework.

Governing Agencies.name: NMFS & USFWS
Governing Agencies.note: ESA Section 7 consultations/BiOps constraining CVP/SWP operations.

Governing Agencies.name: CDFW
Governing Agencies.note: State fish/wildlife authorities and water quality roles (especially where CESA/water quality certifications apply). Often works with Regional Boards; typically part of project compliance teams.
